edits.match: Severe skin reactions are more common in children, in people who reacted to an epilepsy medicine, in those allergic to trimethoprim and in those taking sodium valproate
edits.reason: WRONG: this risk list is the NHS lamotrigine wording, not allopurinol; the NHS allopurinol pages give HLA-B*58:01 / Han Chinese, Thai, Korean, African or Indian origin, previous reaction and kidney/liver/thyroid problems as the risk factors.

notes: NHS excerpt supports SJS description (flu-like then spreading red/purple blistering rash), stopping and seeking urgent help, avoiding new medicines in the first 3 months, and HLA-B*58:01 ethnic risk. Febuxostat boxed warning matches FDA 2019 (legacy ucm URL). Oxypurinol pharmacology is standard. Protected fields unchanged.
